clue.text: Thick liquid covering one in hotel lift

parts.note: thick in the sense of stupid gives dumb

indicators.note: covering says the liquid goes round the numeral for one

parts.note: water is the everyday liquid
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A guest gets stuck with something gooey in the hotel's elevator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thick' looks like a description of the liquid but is a separate piece meaning stupid.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumbwaiter is a small service elevator carrying food and dishes between floors of a hotel or house.

clue.text: Bone turned up in vegan lunch

indicators.note: turned up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bone shows up in a meal meant to be meat-free.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulna is one of the two long bones of the forearm.

clue.text: Fail to justify felon's first conviction

parts.note: to belie is to fail to justify or fulfil, as a hope

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of felon's

explanation.surface: Evidence fails to support a criminal's earliest conviction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conviction' suggests a court verdict; here it means a firmly held opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: A conviction is a firmly held opinion or creed, a strong faith in something.

clue.text: Worried parent drinking whisky and port

indicators.note: drinking says the rearranged letters take in the W
worried means troubled, so the letters of parent are disturbed

parts.note: whisky is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An anxious mother or father drinks whisky and port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' sits as a drink beside whisky, but it is the definition: a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Antwerp is a major Belgian seaport on the Scheldt, among Europe's busiest harbours.

clue.text: Band on road in Mediterranean city

definitions.meaning: a rubber hoop fitted round a wheel that meets the road surface
an ancient Phoenician port in Lebanon on the Mediterranean coast

explanation.definitionFit: The British spelling of a wheel's rubber covering matches the name of the Lebanese coastal city.

clue.text: Explorer, bitter, stopping just short

indicators.note: stopping says the beer plugs a gap inside the shortened word
short says the last letter of the word for just is dropped

parts.note: just means right or fair
bitter is a British type of beer, an ale

explanation.surface: An embittered explorer halts just before reaching his goal.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British style of beer, so it means ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter Raleigh was the Elizabethan explorer and courtier who sailed to the Americas.

clue.text: Severely critical, but course is on anyhow

indicators.note: anyhow means in a haphazard way, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A harsh critic insists that the event will go ahead regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone censorious is quick to find fault and condemn, highly judgemental.

clue.text: Good money Scotsman placed in Post Office — sound investment?

parts.note: the rand is South Africa's currency

indicators.note: placed in says the Scotsman goes inside the abbreviation

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: Good cash deposited by a Scot at the post office: a safe investment?
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' means musical, not safe: a costly instrument is an investment in sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical definition: buying a concert instrument is literally an investment that produces music.

clue.text: Stick close to concierge in block

indicators.note: in says that letter sits inside the word for block

parts.note: to bar is to block

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of the word concierge

explanation.surface: Someone stays near the hotel porter in an apartment block.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick something is to put up with or tolerate it, as in 'I can't stick him'.

clue.text: One-sided varsity man seen around subsequently

indicators.note: seen around says the university and the man are found on either side of the word for afterwards

parts.note: varsity is an old word for university
Al is a man's name, short for Alan or Albert
subsequently means afterwards, at a later time

explanation.surface: A one-sided contest: a university man is spotted about town afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The varsity word and the man's name sit side by side and are split open to take the word for afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A unilateral decision or action is taken by one side alone, without the other party's agreement.

clue.text: Inventor's time at Twickenham recalled

definitions.note: the 's is short for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: recalled, called back, says the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: 'no side' is the referee's call ending a rugby match, and Twickenham is England's rugby stadium

explanation.surface: An inventor's moment at a famous sports ground is remembered.
explanation.walkthrough: Twickenham is the London home of English rugby union; 'no side' is the old term for full time in a rugby match.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was the prolific American inventor of the phonograph and a practical electric light bulb.

clue.text: County town base for leader of Dissenters

parts.note: a bed is a base, as a flower bed or the bed of a machine

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter of Dissenters

explanation.surface: A county town served as the base for the head of the Nonconformists.
explanation.walkthrough: Fitting surface: John Bunyan, the Dissenting preacher, was based in Bedford.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedford is the administrative centre of Bedfordshire, an English county, so it is that county's main town.

clue.text: Hercules, say, sending one aloft in sea vessel

indicators.note: in says the altered strongman sits inside the sea

parts.note: brine is a poetic word for the sea

indicators.note: sending pairs with aloft: the numeral is sent elsewhere
aloft in a down clue means moved higher, towards the start

parts.note: Hercules, the mythical strongman, is an example of a giant
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Hercules hoists a man up in a ship at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'aloft' means higher up the column, so 'sending one aloft' shifts the numeral towards the front of the strongman's word.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigantine is a two-masted sailing ship, a kind of seagoing vessel.

clue.text: Burn or river slow rodent's entered

indicators.note: has entered says the two pieces go inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales
to flag is to tire and slow down
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: A stream or river is where a sluggish rat has got in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burn' looks like a Scottish stream beside 'river', but it is the verb for combustion.
explanation.definitionFit: To deflagrate is to burn away suddenly with great heat and intense flame.

clue.text: Description of 5 perhaps upset maiden

definitions.note: maiden here is an adjective meaning first, as in maiden voyage; the answer is used the same way, as in debut album

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the answer to 5 is a wheel's band, and an inner-tubed type could be described as tubed

explanation.surface: A perhaps-description of something leaves a young woman distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 is TYRE; a tyre with an inner tube is tubed.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a first appearance, as in a maiden speech or a debut performance.

clue.text: Brought in ripe bananas for ultimate self-catering holiday?

indicators.note: in says the word for brought sits inside the reworked letters
bananas means crazy, so the letters of ripe are scrambled

parts.note: got means brought, as in 'got the shopping in'

explanation.surface: Someone packs ripe bananas for a holiday where they cook for themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like fruit to bring along, but it is slang for crazy and signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical definition: an indulgent trip catering entirely to one's own self, ego, is the ultimate self-catering holiday.

clue.text: Chapter in story elevated brilliant success

indicators.note: in says the chapter letter sits inside the reversed word
elevated in a down clue means raised, so read bottom to top

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A chapter of a story is held up as a brilliant success.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat means conspicuous success or acclaim, a dazzling achievement.

clue.text: Resting-place in every church

parts.note: per means each or every, as in 'two per person'

explanation.surface: Somewhere to rest can be found in each church.
explanation.definitionFit: A perch is a place where a bird alights and rests, or any lofty seat.

clue.text: Data's returned concerning UK region

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay

indicators.note: returned says the two pieces are read backwards

parts.note: of means concerning, as in 'tales of the sea'
NI is Northern Ireland, a region of the UK

explanation.surface: Statistics are sent back about a part of the United Kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Info is the informal short form of information, which data are.

clue.text: Fellow attorney maybe closing bars

parts.note: co- is a prefix meaning fellow, as in co-worker
a DA, district attorney, is one kind of attorney

explanation.surface: A colleague, perhaps a lawyer, is shutting down the pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' suggests pubs or prison, but here it means bars of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the concluding passage of a piece of music, its final measures.

clue.text: Daughter, one flirting with this term of endearment, could be dangerous

indicators.note: could be says the letters of the word dangerous can be rearranged into other words

explanation.surface: A daughter calling a flirt 'honey' might be playing a risky game.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: DANGEROUS minus D and ONE leaves letters that rearrange into the answer; 'flirting with this' attaches the answer to the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar is used as an affectionate form of address, like honey or sweetheart.

clue.text: Trench-digger burying knight's bad-tempered dog

indicators.note: burying says the trench-digger encloses the knight

parts.note: a sapper is a military engineer who digs trenches
N is knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: A soldier digging a ditch buries a knight's snappy dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that snaps at people, like an irritable hound, is a snapper.

clue.text: Militant spoke about Conservative

indicators.note: about says the spoke goes round the C

parts.note: a radial is a spoke radiating from a centre

explanation.surface: An activist spoke about the Conservative party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoke' looks like the past of speak but is a noun, a wheel's radial bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A radical advocates thorough political change, so is an extremist or activist.

clue.text: First man allowed to start with Bible books firm

parts.note: Adam was the first man in Genesis

indicators.note: to start means the opening letter of allowed

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: The first human was permitted to begin with scripture, and stood firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant describes someone unyielding and resolute in an opinion, not to be moved.

clue.text: Pancake containing most of fish sauce

indicators.note: containing says the shortened fish goes inside the tortilla

parts.note: a taco is a folded Mexican tortilla, a flat corn pancake

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the fish's name is dropped

parts.note: bass is a fish

explanation.surface: A pancake filled with most of a fish and some sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabasco is a fiery red pepper sauce from Louisiana.

clue.text: Email misdirected by alpha female

indicators.note: misdirected says the letters of Email are sent astray into a new order

parts.note: alpha is A in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An email goes astray, sent by the dominant woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Amelia is a girl's name, so an example of a woman.

clue.text: Plant and vase accepted in reward for service

indicators.note: accepted in says the vase is taken inside the gratuity

parts.note: a tip is money given to reward good service
an urn is a large vase

explanation.surface: A waiter accepts a plant and a vase as a tip.
explanation.definitionFit: The turnip is a plant grown for its white root, eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Book featured dietary component

parts.note: ran means featured, as a newspaper ran a story

explanation.surface: A book featured a component of diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Bran is the husk of cereal grain, eaten for its dietary fibre.

clue.text: This writer's rich source

definitions.meaning: belonging to me, the person writing

explanation.definitionFit: The possessive pronoun of the first person matches the word for an abundant resource or a pit producing ore.

clue.text: Keep barrier in island on hold, and gather within

indicators.note: within says the word for gather sits inside the other pieces
on says the island follows the word for hold

parts.note: to port a rifle is to hold it diagonally across the body
to cull is to gather or pick, as flowers

explanation.surface: Instructions for holding a barrier on an island and rounding people up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' is a castle stronghold, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A portcullis is the heavy grating lowered to block the gateway of a castle or fortress.

clue.text: Line that would make Stead sad?

definitions.note: a line is a short written message, as in 'drop me a line'

parts.note: read the answer's pieces as an instruction: with no T and no E, the word Stead is left as sad

explanation.surface: A remark that would upset someone called Stead.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words, 'no' and the letter pair, and it instructs: remove those letters from Stead.
explanation.definitionFit: A line is a short letter or message, as in 'drop me a line', the same as a brief jotting.

clue.text: In addition, Galen dissected brains

indicators.note: In says the cut-up name goes inside the word for an addition

parts.note: a rider is a clause added to a document or bill

indicators.note: dissected says the letters of Galen are cut apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: Galen, the ancient physician, also cut up brains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In addition' reads as 'also', but 'In' is the insertion signal and 'addition' is the rider on a contract.
explanation.definitionFit: The brains of an operation is its organiser or mastermind, the person who leads the plot.
